rules.title: .NET 7 is no longer supported
rules.summary: .NET 7 (Standard Term Support) reached the end of its support on 2024-05-14. Microsoft no longer ships security or quality fixes for it. The same line applies to the SDK that carries it, so a global.json pinning an SDK 7.0.x is reported too.

sources.title: .NET releases index (channel, support phase, end-of-life date)

constraints: Move the project files, global.json, CI images, and container base images to the same release line; a mix hides the old runtime.
Read the breaking-changes list of each release between the old and new line before raising the target.

steps.title: Raise the target framework
steps.instructions: Change the reported TargetFramework (or TargetFrameworks entry) from the 7.0 line to a supported one, for example net10.0.

steps.title: Raise the SDK pin
steps.instructions: Update the sdk version in global.json to an SDK of the same supported line, or remove the pin if the repository does not need one.

steps.title: Align CI and container images
steps.instructions: Update setup-dotnet versions in CI and the mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet images in Dockerfiles to the new line.

verification.purpose: Confirm the SDK and runtime in use are the intended supported release.
Build and test every project on the new target.

rules.title: WindowsAzure.Storage is deprecated on NuGet
rules.summary: Microsoft marked every version of WindowsAzure.Storage as deprecated (reason: Legacy) because the package has been obsolete since 2023-03-31 and is no longer maintained or monitored. The deprecation names Azure.Storage.Common as the replacement.
rules.replacement: Azure.Storage.Blobs, Azure.Storage.Queues, Azure.Storage.Files.Shares, or Azure.Data.Tables, with Azure.Storage.Common

constraints: Keep the data format and the blob, queue, and table names the same; only the client library changes.

steps.title: Move to the Azure.Storage.* packages
steps.instructions: Replace WindowsAzure.Storage with the package for each service in use (Azure.Storage.Blobs, Azure.Storage.Queues, Azure.Storage.Files.Shares, or Azure.Data.Tables) and update CloudStorageAccount and CloudBlobClient code to the new client types.

verification.purpose: Build and test after the client library change.
